lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: /x/ is 4chan's paranormal board. It began in January 2005 as a photography board and switched to the unexplained in February 2007.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Eight posts, two hours and forty-three minutes. The title borrows from Death Note, the 2003 manga where writing a name in a notebook kills.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: The original post: a poster who says he runs psychic "experiments" has been silent for a week, on the board and on his blog. His last thread has been archived.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: First reply, with theories: real life, no results, boredom, the feds. It wishes he'd published his method.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Second reply, the number: three successes out of eight experiments in October. Huge, it says, like hitting a one-metre target at a thousand metres in a storm.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: A third reply says he keeps writing about failure, as if he expected to win every time. It cites a book, The Forbidden Parapsychology: a 2020 paperback, 112 pages, sold as techniques for influencing people from a distance. The replier says it covers psychic attacks on strangers, not meant to kill.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: The idea is old. Occultist Dion Fortune published Psychic Self-Defence in 1930, and said a psychic attack had caused her own breakdown. In 1942, physiologist Walter Cannon argued in "Voodoo Death" that belief in a curse could kill through fear alone. Later researchers proposed other causes, from slowed heart rate to dehydration.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: At two fifteen, an anon says they didn't think there were others like them. Three minutes later, another notes his blog takes anonymous comments. At two forty-three, a third says they left one.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: The thread never defines a success, never names a target, and shows no reply from him. None of it can be verified.
